title: WPSS/847/2019 of ARVIND KUMAR Vs STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH

paras.text:

COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
02.12.2021 WPSS No. 847 of 2019
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Pankaj Miglani, Advocate, for the
petitioner.
Mr. Gopal Kumar Verma, Addl. CSC,
for the State of U.P.
The late father of the petitioner Mr.
Sudesh Chand, who was working with the
respondent with effect from 1st July 1997, as
Beldar, had met with the sad demise on 11th
August 2018. As a consequence of his death, he
had left behind himself his widow Vimla, two
married daughters, married son and the
petitioner, who claims himself to be unmarried
and unemployed one of the son's of the
deceased and the third daughter Kumari Vikki,
who was unmarried and unemployed.
The petitioner has come up with the
case that as a consequence of the death of his
father late Mr. Sudesh Chand, the petitioner, as
well as his mother had applied for
compassionate appointment by filing an
application, for the grant of compassionate
appointment to the petitioner, as per the
provisions of Dying in Harness Rules of 1974.
But, the claim of the petitioner for grant of
appointment on compassionate grounds has
been rejected by the Executive Engineer, vide
impugned order dated 15th October 2018,
though on the ground that there is no percentage
of quota which has been assigned in the cadre
which are available with the respondent as
against which the petitioner's claim for
appointment could be considered for grant of
compassionate appointment.
The respondents have put in
appearance and have filed their counter affidavit
and particularly the respondents' counsel had

made reference to the implications of Rule 5 of
the Rules, which had provided that in case if
either of the spouse of the deceased is already
employed, in that eventuality, no benefit of
compassionate appointment under the Rules
could be extended to the other dependents of a
deceased employee.
Admittedly, in the case at hand, the
widow of the deceased namely Vimla Devi, she
was already working as a Chawkidar as on the
date of the death of her husband and as such on
the date of the submission of an application for
claiming appointment on compassionate
ground, the same could not be considered in the
light of the provisions contained under Rule 5
of the Rules, as referred to in the counter
affidavit, which had rather created a legal
embargo in considering the claim of the
petitioner for appointment on compassionate
grounds.
In view of the very specific provision
provided under Rule 5, since the spouse was
admittedly employed and working, the
petitioner, though despite being an unmarried
son of the deceased could not be considered for
appointment on compassionate grounds because
the spouse of the deceased was already
working.
The ground taken in the counter
affidavit is in consonance to the specific
provision of a welfare legislation and hence, the
writ petition does not call for any interference
and the same is accordingly dismissed.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 02.12.2021 Mahinder/
